title: Centric's 200-plus own software products make it a competitor as often as a channel
content:
Centric's recorded stack is not a third-party platform at all but 200-plus software products of its own, plus Peppol. The screen's verdict is a single sentence — it competes as often as it would carry you — and that is exactly what a portfolio that size implies: on any given deal the firm is at least as likely to be selling its own module as integrating someone else's layer.

The distinction matters because the partner thesis depends on a firm having a gap it wants filled. A systems integrator carrying a third-party workflow platform has an obvious seam where an append-only record layer can be added without cannibalising anything. A product house has the opposite incentive: whatever the new layer records is a candidate feature for a product it already ships and already bills for.

The practical consequence is that Centric cannot be qualified from stack data alone. Any future approach would have to be scoped to a specific product line where no internal overlap exists, and that scoping work is heavier than the pipeline can currently justify — hence priority 9.
